points.detail: #1: finalize-incomplete (a self-consistent release decision closeout governance finalize record).

finalizeIndex.detail: INDEX-INCOMPLETE: the finalization history has a COVERAGE GAP — zero usable records were considered, the latest usable record is FINALIZE-INCOMPLETE, the incomplete count exceeds the threshold, or `--require-latest-finalized` demanded a finalized latest and did not get one. Complete the missing evidence or supply a coherent latest, then re-index; this is not a coherent history.

reasons.detail: The latest (newest) usable record's OWN verdict is `finalize-incomplete` — its most recent finalization chain had a missing / unusable primary receipt or a missing required related record. Complete the missing evidence, re-finalize the latest governance chain, and re-index before treating the history as finalized.

The number of `finalize-incomplete` records in the window exceeds `--max-incomplete`. A recurring incomplete record means recent releases are not being fully evidenced: complete the missing evidence (or raise `--max-incomplete` if a bounded incomplete backlog is acceptable) before treating the history as consistently finalized.

nextActions.detail: A record in the window is `finalize-incomplete` (a missing / unusable primary receipt or a missing required related record): complete the missing evidence with `worker:release-decision-closeout-governance-finalize-index-trend-finalize` (supply the receipt / required records), re-finalize that release's governance chain, and re-index.

Keep this content-free index as the local release-decision-closeout-governance-finalize-index-trend-finalize-history review SUMMARY. It is NOT a legal audit log, a compliance attestation, an external approval / signature, an identity proof, or a deployment / promotion ledger; keep those separately.

guidance: Wire this as a SCHEDULED or on-demand REVIEW summary (per sprint / quarter), NOT a per-release gate: run `worker:release-decision-closeout-governance-finalize-index-trend-finalize` per release and archive each record, then hand a bounded history (oldest first, newest last) here and render `--text` into a review artifact / `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Fail the review on exit 4 (a blocked / untrustworthy history), surface exit 3 (an open history) and exit 2 (an incomplete history) for review, and treat exit 0 (a coherent history) as consistently finalized — never as an authorization.

Keep the history bounded and explicit: `--max-finalizations=N` caps the newest N records (older records are dropped from the window, and the count dropped is surfaced, never silent); `--max-open=N` / `--max-incomplete=N` (each default 0) tolerate a bounded number of non-finalized OLDER records in the window before the accumulation escalates; `--require-latest-finalized` demands a finalized latest; `--strict-open` escalates any open index to a hard block for a high-assurance review.

Archive this index (and the underlying finalization records) as CI artifacts: it is a content-free review SUMMARY, not a substitute for the records it indexes, nor for your legal audit trail, compliance log, external approval / signing, storage retention, or release-promotion processes — keep each of those in its own dedicated system.

Enforce promotion out of band: this index SUMMARIZES a history of the content-free finalization records supplied, but recording a legal audit trail, obtaining an external approval / signature, proving reviewer identity, and promoting a deployment are operator / CI / legal actions this offline indexer never performs.
caveats: This is a RELEASE DECISION CLOSEOUT GOVERNANCE FINALIZE INDEX: it INGESTS a bounded history of content-free `pdfxyz.release-decision-closeout-governance-finalize-index-trend-finalize/1` finalization records a release pipeline produced, RE-VALIDATES each against ITSELF, and folds them into ONE bounded review verdict + follow-up checklist. It is a local content-free finalization-history INDEX SUMMARY over finalization records — NOT a legal audit log, a compliance attestation, an external approval / signature, an identity proof, or a deployment / promotion ledger.

It is offline and READ-ONLY: it makes NO network call, reads NO secret, bucket, or object, RUNS no gate / index / decision / trend / plan / receipt / closeout / governance / finalize itself, and NEVER signs, approves, publishes, promotes, deploys, notifies, deletes, prunes, uploads, or mutates any record, artifact, object, or deployment. An `indexed` index authorizes nothing; it only reports that the content-free finalization records supplied on THIS host indexed as consistently finalized over the review history.

An `indexed` index REQUIRES a coherent bounded history: the latest usable record `finalized`, no tampered / unreadable record, no blocked record, and the open / incomplete counts within their thresholds. It FAILS CLOSED: a tampered OR unreadable record makes the index `index-invalid` (an untrustworthy input, the TOP precedence); a `finalize-blocked` latest / any blocked record, or a `--strict-open` escalation, makes it `index-blocked`; a `finalize-incomplete` latest / threshold breach, a `--require-latest-finalized` miss, or zero usable records makes it `index-incomplete`; a `finalize-open` latest / threshold breach makes it `index-open`. It never fabricates an `indexed` from thin or untrusted input.

It re-derives each ingested record's rollup from the record's OWN recorded primary-receipt source facets + related-record signals + policy (mirroring the Phase 79 `computeFinalizeIndexTrendFinalize` reducer) and treats a recorded rollup that does not re-derive as a TAMPER (`index-invalid`). This re-derivation is TAMPER-EVIDENCE over content-free data, NOT a cryptographic signature — there is no signing key and no attested identity, so the index proves neither authorship nor approval, and a set of fully self-consistent fabricated records is out of its scope.

It emits only bounded enums, small counts, an ISO stamp, and app-authored prose — so it carries no reviewer name or email, no filename, path, object key, bucket, URL, endpoint, region, job / user id, IP, token, raw ref, raw label, raw note, commit URL, size, byte, or digest, even from a hostile input; it never echoes an ingested record's own stamp, and it never echoes an input file path, even on an error.
It is not malware scanning, sanitization, authorization, cloud validation, or deletion proof of any request or object, and it deletes, uploads, promotes, approves, or mutates nothing.

receipt.disclosure: This is a content-free finalization-history INDEX SUMMARY ONLY — NOT a legal / compliance sign-off, an external approval / signature, an identity proof, a deployment authorization, a promotion ledger, an incident record, or an audit log. It ingests a bounded history of previously produced governance finalization records and records whether the recent release decision closeout governance reads as consistently finalized; it authorizes and proves nothing, and it attests no person's identity.
